<pre-registration>
    <metadata>
        <title>Error Distribution Parameters in Visual Working Memory as Predictors of Visuospatial Cognitive Performance</title>
        <description>An online experiment investigating whether individual differences in visual working memory error distributions, characterized by concentration parameters from circular statistical models, predict performance on mental rotation tasks and correlate with self-reported visual imagery vividness.</description>
        <contributors>Research team to be specified</contributors>

        <license type="select_one">
            <options>
                - CC-By Attribution 4.0 International
            </options>
        </license>

        <subject>Cognitive Psychology, Visual Working Memory, Spatial Cognition, Individual Differences, Psychometrics</subject>
        <tags>visual working memory, mental rotation, spatial cognition, circular statistics, von Mises distribution, individual differences, VVIQ2</tags>
    </metadata>

    <study_information>
        <hypotheses>
H1: Individual differences in visual working memory error distributions, characterized by concentration parameters (κ) from von Mises fits, will predict mental rotation accuracy and reaction times (directional hypothesis: higher κ values predict better MRT performance).

H2: Concentration parameters (κ) will predict VVIQ2 imagery ratings (directional hypothesis: higher κ values predict higher imagery vividness scores).

H3: The relationship between κ and mental rotation performance will be strongest for larger angular disparities where precise spatial transformations are most demanding (directional hypothesis: interaction between κ and rotation angle).

H4: All relationships will persist after controlling for domain-general factors including overall accuracy, response consistency, and engagement metrics (directional hypothesis: κ effects remain significant after covariate control).</hypotheses>
    </study_information>

    <design_plan>
        <study_type type="select_one">
            <options>
                - Observational Study
            </options>
        </study_type>

        <blinding type="select_multiple">
            <options>
                - Personnel who analyze the data collected from the study are not aware of the treatment applied to any given group.
            </options>
        </blinding>
        
        <additional_blinding>Participants are unaware of the specific hypotheses regarding error distribution parameters and their relationship to spatial performance.</additional_blinding>
        <study_design>This is a correlational design examining individual differences across three tasks: Visual Working Memory (VWM) orientation recall, Mental Rotation Task (MRT), and Vividness of Visual Imagery Questionnaire-2 (VVIQ2). The design is within-subjects for all measures, with task order counterbalanced using JavaScript-based randomization. The VWM task uses set sizes 1, 3, and 6 with orientation recall. The MRT includes rotation angles of 0°, 50°, 100°, and 150°. All participants complete all tasks in a single online session.</study_design>
        <randomization>Task order (VWM and MRT) will be counterbalanced across participants using JavaScript-based randomization implemented in the Pavlovia.org platform. Trial order within each task will be randomized for each participant. The VVIQ2 questionnaire is always presented last via SurveyMonkey redirection.</randomization>
    </design_plan>

    <sampling_plan>
        <existing_data type="select_one">
            <options>
                - Registration prior to creation of data
            </options>
        </existing_data>
        
        <data_collection_procedures>Participants will be recruited via Prolific online platform with pre-screening filters for adults aged 18-35 with self-reported normal or corrected-to-normal vision and no hearing deficits. Compensation will be set at minimum £9.00 per hour pro rata based on pilot-tested 40-minute session duration. The experiment will be implemented on Pavlovia.org with automatic redirection to SurveyMonkey for the VVIQ2 questionnaire. Minimum browser dimensions of 768x768 pixels will be enforced. All required metadata (browser, OS, frame rate) and focus loss metrics will be recorded.</data_collection_procedures>
        <sample_size>Target sample size is 240 participants to achieve final analysis sample of approximately 185 participants after anticipated exclusions.</sample_size>
        <sample_size_rationale>Power analysis using pwr package in R determined sample size requirements. For multiple regression (VVIQ2 prediction): target effect size f² = 0.06, 3 predictors, α = 0.05, power = 0.80, yielding n = 185. For mixed-effects models (MRT analysis): approximated as correlation with target r = 0.25, α = 0.05, power = 0.80, yielding n = 122. Final target of 240 includes 30% buffer for anticipated online data collection attrition and exclusions.</sample_size_rationale>
        <stopping_rule>Data collection will continue until target sample size of 240 participants is reached, with over-recruitment by 30% buffer as specified in power analysis to account for exclusions.</stopping_rule>
    </sampling_plan>

    <variables>
        <manipulated_variables>This observational study contains no manipulated variables. All variables are measured individual differences.</manipulated_variables>
        <measured_variables>
Primary predictor: Concentration parameter (κ) from von Mises distribution fitted to individual VWM orientation recall errors using maximum likelihood estimation.

Dependent variables: (1) MRT accuracy (proportion correct) and median reaction times for correct trials, calculated separately for each rotation angle (0°, 50°, 100°, 150°); (2) VVIQ2 total score (sum of 32 items) and eight subscale scores (sum of 4 items per scenario).

Covariates: Mean VWM absolute error, overall MRT accuracy, VWM guess rate from mixture modeling, aggregate focus loss metrics (instances and duration), response time variability, timeout rates, and engagement metrics.

Additional measures: Bias parameter (μ) from von Mises fits, demographic data from Prolific (age, sex), browser metadata, session duration.</measured_variables>
        <indices>Concentration parameter (κ) will be extracted from two-component mixture models fitted to individual VWM orientation recall errors using the 'mixtools' package, incorporating von Mises distribution for memory-based responses and uniform distribution for guesses. VVIQ2 total score calculated as sum of all 32 items, with eight subscale scores as sum of 4 items per scenario. All VVIQ2 scores will be standardized (z-scored) for regression analyses.</indices>
    </variables>

    <analysis_plan>
        <statistical_models>
1. Individual von Mises distributions fitted to VWM orientation recall errors using maximum likelihood estimation via 'circular' package in R, with two-component mixture modeling using 'mixtools' package.

2. Linear mixed-effects models using 'lme4' package testing κ prediction of MRT performance: (a) binomial model for accuracy with fixed effects of κ, rotation angle, and their interaction, random intercepts for participants; (b) linear model for median RTs with same structure.

3. Multiple regression models predicting VVIQ2 scores using 'robustbase' package: separate models for total score and eight subscale scores, with κ as primary predictor and domain-general covariates.

4. Model validation using 5-fold cross-validation comparing von Mises to alternative circular distributions (wrapped normal) via AIC.</statistical_models>
        <transformations>VWM orientation recall errors normalized to ±90° range. VVIQ2 scores standardized (z-scored) for regression analyses. Signed errors converted to absolute errors for summary statistics. No other transformations planned unless assumption violations detected.</transformations>
        <inference_criteria>Two-tailed tests with α = 0.05 for all analyses. Benjamini-Hochberg procedure applied for multiple comparisons across eight VVIQ2 subscales and four MRT rotation angles, controlling False Discovery Rate at 0.05. Effect sizes reported with 95% confidence intervals: Cohen's f² for regressions, partial η² for mixed-model factors. Robust regression techniques employed to handle outliers and assumption violations.</inference_criteria>
        <data_exclusion>Participants excluded based on a priori criteria: (1) Incomplete data across VWM, MRT, and VVIQ2; (2) Timeout rate >20% on VWM or MRT; (3) Accuracy <50% on attention checks (Set Size 1 VWM trials, 0° MRT trials); (4) Invariant VVIQ2 responding (>80% identical responses); (5) Session duration outliers (±3 SD from sample mean); (6) Individual trials with RT <200ms removed from VWM and MRT analyses.</data_exclusion>
        <missing_data>Complete case analysis will be used as all survey questions are required fields. Participants with incomplete task data will be excluded per exclusion criteria above.</missing_data>
        <exploratory_analysis>If primary hypotheses are supported, we will explore: (1) Whether relationships differ between VWM set sizes; (2) Alternative circular distribution fits (wrapped Cauchy); (3) Relationships between subjective session difficulty ratings and κ parameters; (4) Potential sex differences in κ-performance relationships. All exploratory analyses will be clearly labeled as such in reporting.</exploratory_analysis>
    </analysis_plan>

    <other>This research bridges cognitive psychology, psychometrics, and computational modeling by connecting behavioral error distributions to individual differences in spatial abilities. The circular statistical framework draws from directional statistics, while hierarchical modeling incorporates advances from computational cognitive science. Sensitivity analyses will re-run primary models excluding trials identified as guesses to ensure relationships are driven by precision rather than guessing. Model validation will examine residuals and use influence diagnostics (Cook's distance) to assess high-leverage data points.</other>
</pre-registration>
